question:
Let sigma be a bijection of the N physical wires, sigma:Fin N equiv Fin N. Its INDUCED bitstring bijection is R_sigma(b)(w)=b(sigma^{-1}(w)); define P by P|b>=|R_sigma(b)>. Thus P is specifically this wire-induced basis permutation, not an arbitrary permutation of all2^N computational labels. A primitive circuit has chronological matrices U_1,...,U_t, with first-listed gate acting first. Consistently rename each gate's target and each control by sigma, retaining gate kind and angle.

Prove that the renamed circuit realizes P(U_t...U_1)P^{-1}, rather than insertion of a one-sided physical permutation. Justify the single-gate conjugation from the induced bitstring action and show the interior inverse/permutation cancellations through the chronological product. Explain why output-only relabeling fails to preserve products, giving two identity stages and an actual nontrivial involutive wire swap as a witness when N>=2. Include empty circuit and N=0,1 boundaries. Finally assess why the same wire-renaming assertion would be false if P were an arbitrary unrelated basis-label permutation: on one wire compare P=X with a nonzero RY. Distinguish algebraic basis reindexing from a physical SWAP/routing implementation; no hardware routing cost follows for free.
reference_answer:
For a bitstring b, R_sigma(b)(sigma(w))=b(w), so renaming the physical target/control wires transports their stored bits exactly. X flips the renamed target; RY/RZ act with the same2x2 matrix on that target with the same spectator context; CX tests the renamed control and flips the renamed distinct target. Hence each renamed primitive U'_j satisfies U'_j P=P U_j on every basis ket, and U'_j=P U_j P^{-1}. Equivalently its entry at(a,b) is U_j(a composed with sigma,b composed with sigma), matching the source matrix_apply formula. This per-gate statement uses the RELATION between sigma and P; it is not true for an unrelated P merely because P is a basis permutation.

Chronological evaluation multiplies later gates on the left. Therefore U'_t...U'_1=(P U_t P^{-1})...(P U_1 P^{-1})=P(U_t...U_1)P^{-1}, since every interior P^{-1}P cancels. The empty product isI and PIP^{-1}=I, so no extra stage is inserted. For N=0 or1 the wire-bijection group is trivial, P=I, and the theorem reduces to unchanged evaluation; those cases do not supply a nontrivial wire-swap example.

Output-only renaming would assign U_j the matrix P U_j. For two identity stages this gives P^2, while output-only reindexing of their composed identity givesP. At N=2 take sigma swapping the two wires, whose induced P sends|01> to|10> and vice versa, fixes|00>,|11>, is nontrivial and hasP^2=I. Thus P^2!=P, so one-sided reindexing is not multiplicative. For more wires the same swap with all others fixed works.

An arbitrary basis permutation still supports a valid ALGEBRAIC conjugation M->PMP^{-1}. It need not correspond to renaming wires gate-by-gate. On one wire the sole wire permutation is identity, so renaming leaves RY(theta) unchanged. The unrelated basis swapP=X instead obeys X RY(theta) X=RY(-theta) for the standard half-angle rotation [[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]]. At theta=pi/2 the off-diagonal signs differ, so RY(-theta)!=RY(theta). This refutes the original unrestricted reading without contradicting general matrix conjugation.

Both boundary label maps are representational: all input/output labels are consistently changed. This is not an assertion that an arbitrary basis permutation is implementable by physical wire swaps, or that routing on a fixed hardware graph is free. The source eval_gate/eval_circuit proofs certify the induced-wire primitive list under exact matrix semantics; static reading is not a new execution.

Gives the two-identity-stage output-only failure with an induced nontrivial involutive wire swap at N>=2, and handles empty circuit/N=0,1 without inventing a nontrivial wire permutation.
Refutes the unrelated arbitrary-basis P reading on one wire using X RY(theta) X=RY(-theta), e.g.theta=pi/2, and distinguishes representation reindexing from physical SWAP/routing costs.

exposition.core_summary: Wire renaming induces one specific permutation of bitstring labels. Each renamed primitive is conjugated by that permutation, so chronological products telescope; arbitrary unrelated basis permutations are not generally wire renamings.

semantic_steps.claim: The wire bijection induces a specific bitstring permutation, and the renamed gate is conjugated by its matrix P.
Both input and output basis maps make interior P^{-1}P cancel through the chronological product, including the empty case.
Output-only reindexing fails by an actual involutive wire-swap/identity-stage witness; unrelated basis-label permutations require a distinct operation.
